ἐγκολπ-όω ,
A.make full and round, like the folds of a robe,
Orph. A. 1183 (tm.):— Pass. , ἐγκεκολπῶσθαι to be curved into a bay or bays, Arist. Mu. 393a23 :— Med. , put in the fold of one's robe: hence metaph., 'have in one's pocket', “τὴν τοῦ Καίσαρος ἰσχύν”
D.C. 48.52
:— Pass. , to have folded round one, “χιτῶνα ἐνεκεκόλπωτο”
Id. 62.2
: metaph., “ἀρετήν”
Mich. in EN 603.24
.
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
